title: Oracle Sparse-Assembly Representation Tomography
hypothesis: The learned sparse latent representation may still contain a small linear sparse assembly that reconstructs each true functional atom, even though 8-example non-oracle 002B inference failed to discover it. With evaluator access to true sparse coefficients and a large independent oracle probe set, a width r <= 16 decoder should substantially improve held-out functional fidelity over r = 1 while preserving off-support locality if such assemblies exist.

scope.primary_question: Does the learned z contain a small linearly decodable sparse functional assembly, or was 002B failure representation-limited rather than inference-limited?

pretraining.note: Only the sparse model is trained in 002C, but its initialization, data stream, objective, and optimizer schedule are identical to 002/002B.

tomography.fit_objective: Oracle least-squares reconstruction of every true coefficient column s_j from frozen learned z on an iid train probe stream. OMP support selection uses only train-probe moments G=E[z z^T] and C=E[z s^T].
tomography.held_out_rule: All fidelity, leakage, context-ratio, and classification metrics are computed on an independent test probe stream never used for support selection or coefficient fitting.
tomography.sparse_decoder: For each true feature j and each width r, fit h_j = z^T a_j with ||a_j||_0 <= r using deterministic Gram-matrix OMP.
tomography.dense_reference: Fit the full linear oracle decoder B=(G+lambda I)^(-1)C. It is interpretive only and cannot make the sparse-assembly gate pass.

gates.rule: A positive seed requires some fixed width r > 1 to pass every sparse gate on held-out probes. All three formal seeds must pass. Thresholds may not be changed after formal results are observed.

interpretation.sparse_positive: A small sparse linear assembly exists in learned z; 002B failure is primarily an address-inference/sample-complexity problem.
interpretation.dense_only: Sparse gate fails but the dense linear reference reaches the same fidelity/locality thresholds; target atoms remain linearly recoverable but are distributed across a wider latent subspace.
interpretation.linear_negative: Neither sparse widths <= 16 nor the dense linear reference reaches the fidelity/locality thresholds; the current learned z is not a stable linearly writable basis for true atoms.
limits: 002C is oracle representation tomography, not a deployable editor.
A negative result rejects only the frozen linear sparse-assembly hypothesis for the current 002/002B encoder and favorable synthetic world.
OMP is a deterministic sparse approximation algorithm, not an exhaustive combinatorial search over all supports.
The dense reference diagnoses distributed linear recoverability but does not rescue the sparse hypothesis.
002 and 002B frozen outcomes remain unchanged regardless of 002C.
